questions.question: What is the recommended logging practice inside a reusable library?
options: Use getLogger(__name__) and leave handler configuration to the application
Use print() so output is always visible
Attach a FileHandler to the root logger
questions.explanation: Libraries should only create loggers (optionally with a NullHandler); the application configures handlers and levels once at start-up.

questions.question: Why is `log.info("charging %s paise", amount)` preferred over an f-string in the call?
options: f-strings are not allowed in logging calls
It is required for JSON output
The message is only formatted if the record is emitted, and the unformatted template can be grouped by log tools
It makes the log level higher
questions.explanation: Lazy %-style arguments avoid formatting cost for filtered records and keep a stable template for aggregation.

questions.question: Why is a ContextVar better than a thread-local for request IDs in asyncio code?
options: Each asyncio task runs in its own copy of the context, while many tasks share one thread
ContextVars are faster to read than any other variable
ContextVars are automatically sent to OpenTelemetry
questions.explanation: Many concurrent requests can run on the same event-loop thread, so a thread-local would be shared; each task gets its own context copy for ContextVars.

questions.question: What does pairing QueueHandler with QueueListener achieve?
options: It sends logs to multiple processes
It moves slow handler I/O to a background thread so logging calls do not block the caller
questions.explanation: The QueueHandler just enqueues records; the QueueListener's thread performs the slow writes.
